title: Solar sales rep
tagline: Learn to turn cold knocks into signed solar contracts.
setting: Conversations happen on porches and driveways across suburban neighbourhoods, moving from first knock to kitchen-table close.

scenarios.label: Cold knock introduction
scenarios.desc: Open a stranger at the door and earn permission to stay.
scenarios.setup: You stand on the front step of a suburban split-level. The homeowner opens the screen door, squints at your badge, and says: “Yeah? What’s this about?”
scenarios.objective: Earn two minutes to show the satellite roof image on your tablet.

scenarios.label: Kitchen table proposal
scenarios.desc: Walk through design, incentives and finance with decision-makers present.
scenarios.setup: You sit at a pine kitchen table with both spouses. The wife taps the printed layout and says: “Show me how the tax credit actually hits our bank account.”
scenarios.skills: System sizing, incentive math and payment framing
scenarios.objective: Get verbal commitment on the 8.4 kW cash-or-loan choice.
scenarios.moment: Tuesday 7:10 pm, golden hour through west windows

scenarios.label: HOA and roof-age pushback
scenarios.desc: Handle the “my HOA won’t allow it” and “roof needs replacement first” objections.
scenarios.setup: The homeowner leans on the garage door frame, arms crossed, and states: “Board rejected my neighbour’s panels last month, and my shingles are fifteen years old.”
scenarios.skills: HOA packet navigation and roof-partner coordination
scenarios.objective: Schedule the roof inspection and deliver the HOA approval packet.
scenarios.moment: Thursday 4:50 pm, overcast with wind in the trees

buyers.angle: Wants the gist in thirty seconds before her toddler wakes.
Will stress-test every production number you show.
Needs the loan payment to stay under their car note.
Demands IRR spreadsheet before signing anything.
Knows every clause and will make you cite the statute.

objections: My neighbour’s system looks ugly from the street
I’m not staying long enough to break even
The tax credit is a scam, the IRS will claw it back
My roof has five years left, I’m not re-roofing for panels
HOA bylaws section four point two forbids street-visible arrays
Your competitor quoted two grand less for the same kilowatts
I’ll just wait for the new Tesla roof tiles next year
Financing through you means a lien on my house, right?

rubric.label: Door opening
rubric.what: Earns permission to stay with a clear, benefit-first hook in under ten seconds.

rubric.label: Site qualification
rubric.what: Confirms roof orientation, shading, electrical panel and ownership in one smooth flow.

rubric.label: Incentive accuracy
rubric.what: States federal, state and utility incentives with correct percentages, caps and timelines.

rubric.label: Payment framing
rubric.what: Presents cash, loan and PPA options side-by-side with true monthly cost and total ownership.

rubric.label: HOA navigation
rubric.what: Delivers the pre-built approval packet, cites statute, and schedules the board liaison call.

rubric.label: Compliance truth
rubric.what: Never guarantees savings, never implies utility disconnection, discloses all fees and lien rights.

pitfalls: Promising a specific dollar savings without a signed production guarantee.
Skipping the roof-age disclosure that triggers the re-roof clause in the contract.
Filing an HOA application before the homeowner signs the design approval page.
line: Selling rooftop solar door to door

personas.name: Talia Morrison
personas.background: Lives on a quiet cul-de-sac with her husband and two young kids. She is a part-time bookkeeping assistant who is trying to make sustainable upgrades without blowing the family budget.
pushbacks: I wish i could talk longer but my toddler is about to wake up
I’m not staying long enough to break even
My neighbour’s system looks ugly from the street

personas.name: Gideon Shaw
personas.background: Gideon worked thirty‑five years designing photovoltaic mounting systems before retiring. He now walks the neighbourhood on foot, testing every claim a installer makes against his own spreadsheets.
pushbacks: Your payback estimate ignores degradation rates, and it won’t hold up to a 600 kWh‑per‑day load
The tax credit is a temporary clause; the IRS can retroactively revoke it if you miss the filing window
If the HOA has a clause that bans visible arrays, your permit will be void on day one

personas.name: Cory Sheffield
personas.background: Cory and her partner earn good money but every dollar gets tracked tightly. They’d rather save than spend on anything that feels like waste.
cares_about: monthly loan payment staying below their car note
not letting the system look bulky on the roof
getting the paperwork done before tax season
pushbacks: I’m not tearing up my roof for a panel that might not save us much
If the tax credit disappears next year we’ll have paid extra for nothing
The roof looks odd enough already we can’t add something that doesn’t blend
wins_over: a payment that fits neatly inside their current budget
a design that matches the existing roof angles
a quick paperwork turnaround before the tax deadline

personas.name: Rafael Goode
personas.background: Rafael owns three small apartments in the area. He sees solar as another income stream and wants clear numbers before he adds another contract.
pushbacks: The payback period is longer than my renovation timeline, so I’m out
I need to see a verified IRR model before I commit to anything else
If the tax credit disappears next year, the math falls apart for me

personas.name: Lila Mendez
personas.background: Serves on her neighborhood board for twelve years, once denied a condo conversion. Publishes a monthly checklist of violation rules.
pushbacks: That array violates clause four two of the bylaws, plain and simple
How do you prove the panels won’t drop property values?
Show me the audit trail for your tax-credit filing
